title: imap: X-USENET-IPFS-VERIFY command for operator signature verification
description:
Why: The NNTP reader exposes XVERIFY <message-id> <expected-cid> [SIG] to let clients confirm a message's CID and operator Ed25519 signature. The IMAP OBJECTID extension (stoa-89c2165e) already surfaces the CID as EMAILID, so CID lookup is covered. Signature verification has no natural home in standard IMAP and needs a custom command.

What:
1. Implement X-USENET-IPFS-VERIFY as a custom IMAP command (RFC 3501 §6 allows X-prefixed commands). Syntax:
     X-USENET-IPFS-VERIFY <uid> [CID <expected-cid>] [SIG]
   Response codes (mirroring NNTP XVERIFY):
     - OK VERIFIED: CID matches and (if SIG requested) signature valid
     - NO [CIDMISMATCH]: CID does not match expected
     - NO [SIGFAIL]: signature verification failed
     - NO [NOTFOUND]: UID not found
2. Advertise X-USENET-IPFS-VERIFY in CAPABILITY so clients can detect support.
3. Also return X-USENET-IPFS-CID and X-USENET-IPFS-SIG as FETCH data items (alongside the standard article headers), so clients that do a FETCH BODY[HEADER] get the usenet-ipfs metadata in the normal header block without a separate command.

Standard IMAP clients that do not send X-USENET-IPFS-VERIFY and do not request the custom FETCH items are completely unaffected.
notes: RESOLVED via JMAP: The blob download (GET /jmap/download/{accountId}/{CID}/{name}) already returns the full article bytes including X-Usenet-IPFS-Sig header. Additionally, stoa-f8d13298 implements exposing the signature as x-usenet-ipfs-sig in Email/get responses. The IMAP X-command path remains blocked. Superseded by 3am for the JMAP path.
